observed_before_declaration: The published Turner algorithm permits at most one collision opportunity per particle and species timestep, whereas the historical AuroraPIC Turner campaigns used the production Poisson clock. At the locked Case 1 majorants, Poisson mean opportunities exceed the Turner Bernoulli probabilities by 1.3891 percent for electrons and 1.1103 percent for ions.

reference.paper: M. M. Turner et al., Physics of Plasmas 20, 013507 (2013)
reference.prescription: Equations 4-5 and surrounding text: test once per timestep, with probability 1-exp(-nu_max*dt), and permit at most one collision.

decision_rule.implementation_pass: The ensemble-mean Poisson/single candidate ratio is inside the preregistered interval and every execution/resource/finite-value gate passes.
decision_rule.turner_bias_direction_supported: In addition to implementation pass, single_bernoulli reduces ensemble-mean ionization and integrated ion density relative to poisson_clock, the direction needed to reduce AuroraPIC's positive Turner density bias.
decision_rule.turner_bias_direction_not_supported: Implementation passes but either ensemble-mean ionization or integrated ion density does not decrease.
decision_rule.failure: The candidate-ratio or execution integrity gate fails.

claim_boundary: This paired 32-cycle continuation identifies the immediate response to the collision-opportunity convention from one common stationary particle state across three RNG seeds. It is not a fresh 1280-cycle Turner realization, a formal published-density comparison, an equilibrium sensitivity result, or experimental validation.
